gaps.sentence: Have we got ___ eggs for breakfast?
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in neutral questions; 'none' cannot stand before a noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: You can park on ___ side of the street.
gaps.hint: singular noun meaning 'this one or that one'
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means one side or the other (both are allowed); 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: He has lived in Berlin and Prague, and loves ___ cities.
gaps.explanation: 'Both cities' refers to the two cities mentioned; 'all' would suggest three or more.

gaps.sentence: There are plenty ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.hint: 'plenty' is always followed by this preposition before a noun
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of + noun' is the fixed pattern; no other preposition follows 'plenty'.
